extra.message: User input from sqli['username'] is inserted directly into SQL query via f-string without parameterization. This allows SQL injection attacks to extract or modify data.

User-supplied URL is passed directly to requests.get() without validation. An attacker can specify arbitrary URLs (e.g., file:///, http://localhost, cloud metadata endpoints) and the server will make requests on their behalf.
User input is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string. Malicious template expressions (e.g., {{config.__class__.__init__.__globals__}}) can be executed, leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (SSTI)

extra.message: User input from request body is returned directly in JSON response without sanitization. If this data is later rendered in HTML without escaping, it enables reflected XSS attacks.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User-supplied filename is used directly in open() without any path validation or sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to traverse directories and read arbitrary files (e.g., /etc/passwd).
User-controlled Host header value is directly reflected in the response body. An attacker can inject HTTP headers or redirect users to malicious sites via malicious Host values.
Flask application is running with debug=True. The interactive debugger exposes a web-based console that can execute arbitrary Python code, providing full remote code execution capability.
Hardcoded credentials (admin/admin) are inserted into the database. If authentication is not implemented, attackers can access the admin account directly.
